To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the conductance-voltage curves of in-situ, a-axis YBCo/Au junctions exhibit a peak structure at T=4K, with a dip in the middle of the peak structure.
the conductance-voltage characteristic of a-axis YBa/sup 2/Cu/sup 3/O/sub /spl delta// (a-YBCO) thin film/Au junctions has a peak structure at low bias and that the peak has a dip at the middle.

the interface resistivity of in-situ YBCO/AU junctions is about an order of magnitudes lower than that of in-situ c-axis YBCo/noble-metal junction and that the conductance-voltage characteristic of the a-axis YBA/sub 2/CU/sub 3/O/sup 7-/spl deltam/Au junctions has a dip in the middle of the peak structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of superconducting YBCO/natural oxide interface junctions and their potential for use in superconducting devices.
the fabrication and characterization of a-axis YBa /sub 2/Cu /sub 3/O /sub 7- /spl delta//noble metal junctions.
the fabrication of a-axis YBC0 thin films and junctions with gold counter electrodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the a-axis YBa/sup 2/Cu/sup 3/ O/sup 7-/spl deltam/Au interfaces are not superconducting, but the junctions are characterized by a low interface resistance and a conductance-voltage characteristic which is not consistent with a simple tunneling model.
the a-axis YBa/sup 2/Cu/sup 3/O/sup 7-/spl deltam/ Au interface is a good candidate for the development of high quality, high critical current density, low noise SQUIDs and bolometers.
the interface conductance-voltages characteristics of a-axis YBC0/Au junctions are very similar to those of c-axis YBC0/normal-metal junctions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interface resistance is reduced by an order of magnitude, the low bias conductance is enhanced by an order of maginitude, and the interface is less sensitive to thermal cycling.
in-situ deposited a-axis YBC0/Au junctions have a lower interface resistance than nominal c-axis YBAC/Au junctions and the a-axis junctions exhibit a unique conductance-voltage characteristic.
the conductance-voltage curves for in-situ YBCO/AU junctions are similar to those for the c-axis YBCo/noble-metal junction, but the interface resistance is an order of magnitude higher.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a-axis YBCOs can be made to form good interfaces with noble metals.
the conductance-voltage behavior of the a-axis YBaCuO/Au interface junctions can be explained by the same mechanism that explains c-axis YBaCu0/Au interface junction behavior.
the a-axis YBaCuO/Au interfaces are promising for applications in superconductor-based devices.
